# Description

Adds **downgrade protection** to the manually-promoted, tag-based deploy tiers

environment's last recorded deployed tag and **blocks** a push whose tag is *older*
than what's live; after a successful push it **records** the deployed tag.

Why the recording step: on the GitHub **Team** plan, a deploy's auto-created
Deployment records the *trigger* ref (the default branch), not the deployed tag — so
we record the tag ourselves (an explicit GitHub Deployment) and read it back to compare.

`dev` and `sit` are the continuous auto tiers (no human-picked tag — `dev` deploys

50-## 2. Contentful
51-
52-1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
53:2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). Not yet confirmed is the split on pages that compose both: which editorial blocks appear on the PDP and PLP and whether any are authored in SFCC Page Designer rather than Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu carries Contentful-authored promotional tiles alongside the SFCC category tree. Zimmermann and merchandising to confirm the per-surface split so the PDP, PLP, and navigation components can be built against a fixed data-source contract. The working assumption is captured in the content-ownership boundary table in the Contentful integration design (§1).
54-3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provision the Space and supply per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be exercised against a real Contentful environment.
55-
56-## 3. MuleSoft
57-
58-1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
59-2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
60-3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).
61-4. **CAI-023 — warehouse + boutique stock aggregation for browse-level availability.** Confirm whether MuleSoft can deliver a pre-aggregated available-to-promise figure combining warehouse and eligible boutique stock, to drive the Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock states on PDP and PLP. If MuleSoft cannot pre-aggregate, the storefront must decide whether to request both sources separately and aggregate client-side (extra round-trip) or fall back to SFCC-only inventory. This is distinct from the cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) and the Find in Boutique flyout (CAI-038), both of which have their own endpoints. **Owner:** Integration team (Tryzens / MuleSoft).

Findings below. One framing note up front: you're already on `fix/footer-tablet-wide-breakpoint` with the change applied (`footer.css.ts` + `footerShared.ts` modified), so the lint run in item 6 is your working tree, not a clean develop — details there.

---

## 1. Real PR body convention

**Two distinct conventions exist.** Four of the five PRs follow the template; **#62 does not**.

**Template-following (#46, #47, #59, #64)** — `#` H1 headings, in this order:

```
# Description
# Linked
# Squad ownership
# Types of Changes
# Changes
# How to test-drive this PR
# Protection-tier check
# Testing
```
Then, only when relevant: `# Accessibility`, `# Localisation`, `# Known gaps and follow-ups` (#64), `# Note on file naming` (#47).

**#62 is the outlier** — `## Summary` / `## Test plan` only, plus a `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code]` footer. It's the most recent merge (2026-08-27T02:39Z) but it's the odd one out; don't model on it.

### The "Linked" section — how it actually references Jira/Confluence

The template prescribes four bullets (`PRD / requirement:`, `Sprint:`, `Figma:`, `Ticket: SFCC-`). **No merged PR uses that shape.** The real convention is **two bullets, `Ticket:` first, `Sprint:` last**, with Figma/Confluence folded *into* the Ticket bullet as prose:

- Jira key is **bolded inline** with a parenthetical title: `**SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI)`, `**SFCC-89** (PDP — static product information)`
- Confluence is cited as *italic page title* + bare numeric page ID: `Confluence *Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)* (335216656)` — no URL
- Figma is cited as *italic file name* + raw node IDs: `Figma *Zimmermann_Designs* — desktop PDP \`3093:67151\``
- Platform PRs with no Jira story name the **epic** instead: `tag-based promotion rollout under epic **SFCC-1** (Platform Setup & Environments)`
- Sprint format drifts: `SFCC Sprint 2` (#46, #47) vs `SFCC — Sprint 3` (#59, #64). The em-dash form is the newer one.

**Representative body, verbatim (#59 — the footer PR, your closest precedent):**

```markdown
# Linked

- Ticket: **SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI). Design: Figma *Zimmermann_Design_System_2026*;
  footer frames signed off with Dani & Vicky (2026-07-07). Test cases SFCC-T116 – SFCC-T122
- Sprint: SFCC — Sprint 3

# Squad ownership

- [x] Squad B

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
```

**Other template-vs-reality gaps:**
- `# Squad ownership` — template lists 4 checkboxes to tick one; #46/#47/#59 **delete the unticked lines entirely** and show only the ticked one. #64 keeps all four.
- `# Testing` — template is a fixed 7-item checklist; real PRs **rewrite the list**, appending results inline (`— clean`, `— 379 passed / 25 files`) and adding non-template rows (Box model, Figma geometry, Local CodeRabbit, `/code-quality` audit). Non-applicable items become `- N/A: …` bullets rather than unticked boxes.
- Unresolved contradictions are surfaced as `>` blockquote callouts rather than silently decided — see #64's "**Ownership contradiction, flagged not resolved.**"

Template: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`

## 2. Commit message convention

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/hooks/commit-msg`

Line 15 is the whole enforcement:

```bash
pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$'
```

- **Types (11, exhaustive):** `feat fix docs style refactor perf test build ci chore upstream-sync` (`upstream-sync` is Zimmermann-specific)
- **Scope:** optional; parenthesised; **lowercase only** — `[a-z0-9/._-]+`. No uppercase, no spaces. So `fix(footer)` is valid, `fix(SFCC-123)` is **rejected** (uppercase). Jira keys go in the *subject*, not the scope.
- **Length:** description is **1–100 chars** after `: `. Note the regex is anchored `^...$` against the *whole message*, so this effectively caps the subject line; the `.` class doesn't match newlines under `grep -E`, so multi-line bodies pass via the subject line only.
- **Bypass (line 10):** messages starting with `Merge`, `Revert`, `fixup!`, `squash!`, or `WIP` skip validation entirely.

### Last 15 subjects on develop

## 3. Is there an open Jira ticket for footer responsive/tablet?

- `gh pr list --search "footer"` returns 7 PRs. The only footer-scoped keys are **SFCC-55** (#55 CLOSED, #59 MERGED — both `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`). Nothing responsive/tablet-specific.

- No `860` anywhere in `.docs/` or `.claude/`. The only two `860` occurrences in `overrides/` are the two comment lines you just wrote in `footerShared.ts:19,24`.

Closest available anchors if you want *something* in `# Linked`: **SFCC-55** (parent story, merged in #59 — this is a defect in what that shipped) and the SFCC-723 precedent from #64, where an out-of-scope layout-geometry gap got its own ticket. #64 also demonstrates the accepted pattern for genuinely ticketless work — a prose `Ticket:` bullet naming the epic instead of a key.

## 4. Protection-tier block format

The section is `# Protection-tier check`. Real PRs **replace the template's four checkboxes with a `>` blockquote narrative**, then optionally keep a few `- [x]` lines. Two shapes:

**Shape A — Tier 1 touched (#59, verbatim):**

```markdown

> ⚠️ **Tier 1** — `.storybook/{main.js,preview.tsx}` (test config, **Integration-owned**)
> for serving and mounting the self-hosted fonts; `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`

> `theme/foundation/sizes.ts` (design system, **UI-Designer-owned**) — whitespace only,
> and it now diffs to **zero** against `develop`.

>

**Shape B — no Tier 1 (#64, verbatim) — this is your case:**

>

```

      `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`)

**Your two files:**
- `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts` → **Tier 2**, UI-Designer-owned. `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md:26` covers `overrides/app/theme/components/`, and lines 41–43 name `footerShared.ts` explicitly as *staying* Tier 2 because it's a "genuinely cross-component shared value" that co-location doesn't cover.

- Neither is Tier 1 — `frozenFiles.md:12-24` freezes only `theme/foundation/`, and `:44` explicitly puts `theme/components/` at Tier 2.
- Footer is **Squad A territory** (`.claude/rules/squadA.md`), but that file says `footer/` is *"shared shell — notify Squad B before any change."* #59 shipped it as Squad B. Expect to tick **Cross-squad**.

## 5. Footer Storybook `play` functions vs. the 860px removal

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx` — 6 stories, **4 with `play`**:

| Story | Line | `play` asserts | Width-sensitive? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Default` | :31 | `target`/`rel="noopener noreferrer"`/accessible name on WhatsApp; no `target` on tel:/mailto: | **No** — attributes only |
| `Subscribed` | :49 | *(none)* | n/a |
| `SubscribeSubmit` | :69 | types email → modal opens → fills names → Continue → dialog gone, "temporarily unavailable" shown | **No** — roles + text |
| `SubscribeModalOpen` | :110 | `body.style.overflow` lock, focus entry, Tab trap both directions, Escape, focus restore | **No** — focus/DOM only |
| `ContactChannelFallbacks` | :189 | absent/unsafe channels render as `role="img"` span, not link | **No** |
| `SubscribePlaceholder` | :217 | **measures `getBoundingClientRect().height`** on `footer[role="contentinfo"]` and the `[aria-live]` slot, before/after submit | **Yes — but only relatively** |

**Only `SubscribePlaceholder` (:217-261) touches layout**, and it is safe. It is a **before/after equality assertion at a single unchanged viewport** — it never asserts an absolute width, height, gap, or breakpoint. Both measurements happen inside one `play` at one width, so whatever gap value the media queries resolve to is identical on both sides of the comparison.

The two guards it does make are floor checks, not size checks (:236-237):
```ts
await expect(slotBefore).toBeGreaterThan(0);
await expect(heightBefore).toBeGreaterThan(0);
```
Removing a `gap` step cannot drive either to 0.

The comment at :251-254 is the one place width is mentioned, and it argues *for* the assertion's robustness across widths:
> `// measurably at every viewport, and visibly on mobile where the columns stack and the footer itself moves.`
> `// Asserted on the slot as well as the footer: at desktop widths the taller site-map column sets the row height, so a footer-only check passes even when the column has shifted.`

**Also confirming no viewport is configured anywhere**, so the 860px band is never exercised: `.storybook/main.js:13-17` registers only `addon-webpack5-compiler-babel`, `addon-links`, `addon-docs`, `addon-a11y` — **no `@storybook/addon-viewport`**. `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets `parameters` (:34) and `a11y` (:42) but no `viewport`/`globals` width. There is **no `.storybook/test-runner.js`** and **no `test-storybook` script in `package.json`** (PRs invoke `npx test-storybook`), so the runner uses Playwright's default **1280×720** — above `BP.desktop` (64em/1024px), where the `desktop` rule (`gap: 0`) wins regardless. The `tabletWide` rule was **never active in any Storybook run**.

**Verdict: zero play functions at risk.** Note the corollary for your PR body — no automated test covers the 768–1024 band at all, so the "~124px → ~68px" measurement in your `footerShared.ts` comment is developer-verified only and should be stated as such in `# Testing` (the #64 precedent for this is its `- **Not verified: …**` bullet).
